title: Justice Among the Merchants
intro: A figure stood before a people consumed by the lure of profit, calling them to honesty and fairness in their dealings. This servant of Allah warned against giving short measure and tampering with the scales. The people refused to listen, threatening to banish this individual from their land. The earth itself would rise up in judgment against them. Who is this figure that stood for justice among the merchants?
clues: I was sent as a messenger to a people who were deeply immersed in trade and commerce.
My people gave short measure when weighing goods for others.
They threatened to expel me from the land if I persisted in calling them to faith.
I am remembered as the most eloquent speaker among the prophets.
My people were seized by a violent earthquake that left them lifeless in their homes.
I was sent to the people of Madyan in the northern Hijaz.

arabic: قَالُوا۟ يَـٰشُعَيْبُ أَصَلَوٰتُكَ تَأْمُرُكَ أَن نَّتْرُكَ مَا يَعْبُدُ ءَابَآؤُنَآ أَوْ أَن نَّفْعَلَ فِىٓ أَمْوَٰلِنَا مَا نَشَـٰٓؤُا۟ ۖ إِنَّكَ لَأَنتَ ٱلْحَلِيمُ ٱلرَّشِيدُ
verse: They said, "O Shuʿayb, does your prayer [i.e., religion] command you that we should leave what our fathers worship or not do with our wealth what we please? Indeed, you are the forbearing, the discerning!" (11:87)
